text:
Alex: Quick heads-up — I uploaded a couple of recent nsys + perfetto captures from the KV-prefetch regression. Kernel timeline shows the prefetch kernels interleaving with small compute kernels and causing a stall spike.

Priya: Can you paste the nsys command you ran? I want to reproduce locally. :thinking_face:

Alex: nsys profile -o kv-prefetch-run --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt python run_trace.py --batch 8 --seq 2048
Output attached as run.kv-prefetch-run.qdrep (uploaded to perf-bucket).

Jordan: Looked at the perfetto timeline — the root cause seems to be coarse NVTX ranges. We have a single "KV_CACHE" range that covers both read and async prefetch. Perf tools can't attribute the tiny kernels correctly.

Sam: Agree. Proposal: add finer-grained NVTX ranges specifically for (1) kv:lookup (fast sync read), (2) kv:prefetch_async (dispatch), and (3) kv:commit/miss-handling. Keeps span length short so perf timeline shows the short kernels.

Priya: +1. Also we should pick a compact naming scheme to avoid long strings in the trace UI. Suggest: rt:rq:<rid>:kv:<op> where <op> in {lookup,prefetch,miss}. Example: nvtxRangePushA("rt:rq:42:kv:prefetch").

Alex: That scheme looks good. Two practical concerns: overhead of pushing more NVTX ranges, and how to handle aggregated/batched requests where multiple logical requests share a kernel. Any ideas?

Jordan: For overhead, we measured nvtx push/pop cost ~ tens of ns in microbenchmarks — acceptable for our kernels which are >10us. We should gate NVTX by a runtime flag and enable it only on debug/perf runs or when perf-bot injects sampling.

Sam: For batching, propose per-batch outer range plus per-request inner ranges when we have request IDs. e.g.: nvtxRangePushA("rt:batch:23"); for per-request: nvtxRangePushA("rt:rq:42:kv:lookup"); then pop inner, continue batch. That lets perf viewers collapse by batch or inspect per-request.

Priya: One more: keep names under ~128 chars and avoid spaces/colons collisions in UI. Use colons to namespace, slashes cause issues in some viewers.

InfraBot: perf-bot noticed heavy disk IO during run.kv-prefetch-run.qdrep. Potential correlation: prefetch triggers pagefaults which serialize kernels. File: perf-bucket/run.kv-prefetch-run.log

Alex: Good call, @InfraBot — disk activity could explain stalls. I'll add a small NVTX disk IO range around the prefetch path too: nvtxRangePushA("rt:rq:42:kv:prefetch:io").

Jordan: Can we add metrics to the console to show "kv-prefetch overlap ratio"? If prefetch kernels overlap more than X ms with compute, create an alert.

Priya: I'll add a lightweight metric in the runtime: counters for prefetch_inflight_time and compute_overlap_time. Then Redwood Console can graph it per model.

Sam: I'll open a tiny PR with the NVTX naming helpers and an opt-in env var (REDWOOD_NVTX=1). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/____ (WIP) :thumbsup:

Alex: Thanks — next steps: (1) land NVTX helpers (Sam), (2) run nsys+perfetto with REDWOOD_NVTX=1 on the failing workload (me), (3) Priya wires metrics into console dashboard. We'll reconvene after one successful capture.

perf-bot: run scheduled: nightly-kv-prefetch-178 -> status queued (will run with REDWOOD_NVTX=1).

Sam: if anyone needs the naming helper API: helper in C++:
```
inline void nvtx_span_push_fmt(const char* fmt, int id, const char* op) {
  char buf[128];
  snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), fmt, id, op); // fmt: "rt:rq:%d:kv:%s"
  nvtxRangePushA(buf);
}
```

Priya: Nice. Also add a small unit-test to ensure the helper truncates gracefully when name exceeds buffer.

Alex: Great thread. Filing follow-up issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/perf-kv-trace. Meeting in two days to review capture. :calendar:
